10 gifts for adults who enjoy building aircraft models

Model builders tend to have specific preferences about scale, subject, and techniques. Buying the biggest kit available can create a project they never wanted. These ten gift ideas support the hobby at different stages, from choosing a new subject to displaying a finished build.

By Pilot Gift Guide · How we choose

IN THIS GUIDEHow to chooseThe listRelated guides

How to choose

Ask what scale they work in, what is already in their stash, and whether they enjoy assembly, painting, or detailing most. Check the tools and materials a kit requires. Any chemicals or sharp tools should be selected by the recipient for their workspace and experience.

The list

Our selections prioritize personal relevance, usefulness, and fit for the recipient. Named products and destinations link to official sources where applicable.

  1. 1

    Exact wish-list kit

    The safest substantial purchase is the precise kit they requested. Manufacturer, scale, and edition can matter even when the aircraft name is identical.

  2. 2

    Display case contribution

    A finished model needs protection and room. Measure wingspan, height, base, and any open panels before ordering a case.

  3. 3

    Reference photo book

    Choose a book about the aircraft they are building. Clear, relevant reference images can be more useful than a broad aviation overview.

  4. 4

    Decal storage folder

    A suitable organizer can help keep existing supplies orderly. Ask about sheet sizes and the way they already store delicate materials.

  5. 5

    Model photography backdrop

    A simple backdrop supports sharing finished work. Match the size to their models and choose a surface they can store conveniently.

  6. 6

    Work-in-progress storage

    A covered project box can protect unfinished work between sessions. Measure parts and ask how much bench space is available.

  7. 7

    Requested tool replacement

    Replace one worn tool with the exact preferred version. Avoid a large beginner tool set for someone with an established setup.

  8. 8

    Custom model plaque

    An understated plaque can identify a finished subject. Confirm the aircraft details and let the builder decide whether it belongs on their display.

  9. 9

    Model-show outing

    Plan transport and time for an event they want to attend. Check current dates and access rather than assuming an annual event is unchanged.

  10. 10

    Uninterrupted building afternoon

    Arrange practical time for the hobby, perhaps with a meal afterward. This can be more useful than adding another unopened box to the collection.

These are editorial recommendations and planning ideas, not hands-on test results. Read how we choose our picks.
